g.text: The lens reads which item is at the bridge, not where its locker sits

text.style: font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #666666

g.text: An address swap and an item change read through the J++ lens, against 200 random vectors of the same size
Grey: the 95% range of the 200 random vectors (2.5th to 97.5th percentile): on the left one per change, on
that change's word, 2 units wide by construction (about ±1); on the right one for both changes.
Left: z = (ln m − ln r) / w, with r the median rank over the cases of the new item's name (item change) or of
the best-ranked of 15 position words such as first, next, 2 (address swap), m the random vectors' median of
the same, w half their 95% range of ln rank.
Asked to say the position, the 27B never has the right ordinal word in the lens's top five (0.00, n = 200),
yet loses 0.28 of its reports without the address (extra loss, beyond a random part).
